question.knowledge_point: Solving Trigonometric Equations Involving Cosecant with Special Angles
question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\text{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

Since $\frac{\pi }{3}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

Our first solution lies in the  first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978818/assets/4cbf970747a9eddbcffe6fd3ba46d13c43e5f17ca56e52747c797229dbc74d48.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are $x=\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{2\pi }{3}.$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot \frac{2\pi }{3}=\frac{2{\pi }^{2}}{9}.
$$
